flows.title: The Zotero save button doesn't appear in my browser
flows.hint: For Chrome/Edge, Firefox or Safari. Usually fixed by pinning or reinstalling the connector — a few short steps.
flows.based_on: C1 in the support analysis (20 questions); official KB topic no_toolbar_button

q-browser.heading: Which browser are you using?
q-browser.body: The fix depends on how your browser manages toolbar extensions.

fix-chromium.heading: Pin the Zotero extension in Chrome or Edge
fix-chromium.body:
1. Click the puzzle-piece icon (Chrome) or the extensions icon (Edge) in the toolbar.
  2. Find Zotero Connector and click the pin so it always shows. In Edge, choose Show in Toolbar.
  3. If Zotero is not in the list at all, install it from the Zotero download page and confirm the browser's install prompt.

fix-chromium-reinstall.heading: Reinstall the connector, then reset the browser if needed
fix-chromium-reinstall.body:
1. In the browser's extensions page, remove Zotero Connector.
  2. Install it again from the Zotero download page.
  3. If it is enabled but still invisible, the official docs suggest resetting Chrome/Edge settings (Settings → Reset) — extensions come back, this clears configuration that can hide them.

fix-firefox.heading: Find and pin the button in Firefox
fix-firefox.body:
1. Open the extensions panel (puzzle-piece icon). If Zotero is there, pin it via the gear icon.
  2. Otherwise check the overflow menu (») — Firefox often stows it there; resizing the address bar can reveal it.
  3. If it is in neither place, reinstall from the download page. As a last resort the official docs suggest testing in a new Firefox profile — a broken profile is a known cause.

fix-safari.heading: Enable the Zotero Connector in Safari's extension settings
fix-safari.body:
1. Open Safari → Settings → Extensions.
  2. Select Zotero Connector and tick Enable Zotero Connector.
  3. Also grant it permission For other websites if you save from many sites.
  4. If Zotero is not listed, install the Safari connector from the download page (it ships with the macOS app and needs enabling once).

exit-safari.heading: Safari needs the official compatibility guide
exit-safari.body: Safari's extension handling changes between macOS versions and is a recurring topic in the support data (row #73: connector registered but missing from Safari's extension list). Zotero keeps a dedicated page for exactly this:
exit-safari.link_label: Official guide: Zotero Connector and Safari

exit-forum.heading: This one goes to the official forum
exit-forum.body: A still-invisible button after a clean reinstall is usually browser-specific configuration the community has seen before. Search the forum for your browser plus "save button", and include your browser version if you post.

done-solved.heading: The save button is back
done-solved.body: Next: capture your first sources with it — lesson 2: Save your first sources from the web.

flows.title: Saving fails: "Zotero is unavailable" — or items/PDFs never appear
flows.hint: Three distinct failure modes with different fixes: app closed, item saved out of sight, or PDF missing.
flows.based_on: C1; rows #86, #91, #135 in the support analysis

q-symptom.heading: What exactly happens when you save?
q-symptom.body: These are three different problems with three different fixes.

options.label: A message says Zotero is unavailable (or nothing happens)
It says it saved, but no item appears in Zotero
The item appears, but the PDF is missing

fix-unavailable.heading: The connector can't reach the Zotero app — check the desktop app first
fix-unavailable.body:
1. Is the Zotero desktop app open? The browser extension talks to the app on your computer (local port 23119). If the app is closed, open it and save again.
  2. Restart your browser and retry.
  3. Still failing? Open http://127.0.0.1:23119/connector/ping in the browser — it should say “Zotero is running”. If it does but saving still fails, an extension blocker (AdBlock, NoScript, Privacy Badger…) is the usual suspect: disable blockers for 127.0.0.1 and retry.
  4. If the ping fails in every browser, exclude 127.0.0.1 from proxy/VPN settings or check security software — details in the official KB.

fix-not-appearing.heading: The item saved — but where? Check the right library view
fix-not-appearing.body:
1. In Zotero, click My Library itself (not a subcollection) and sort by Date Added. The item is usually there — saved into the currently selected collection or the root.
  2. Check whether you were saving into a group library by mistake; the save popup names the destination.
  3. Restart Zotero. In rare cases the connector reports success but the app needs a restart to show the queue — if a restart is needed every time, that's a forum topic (row #86 in the support data).

fix-pdf-missing.heading: Get the PDF: save from the article page, or attach it yourself
fix-pdf-missing.body:
1. Save from the article's landing page (where the abstract is), not from inside the PDF viewer. Translators on some sites — JSTOR is a known case (row #91 in the support data) — attach PDFs far more reliably from the landing page.
  2. Already have the PDF on disk? Drag it onto the item in Zotero to attach it (lesson 3 covers parent items).
  3. Some publishers simply don't allow automatic PDF download. The record is still complete — get the PDF from your library's access and drag it in. That's a limitation, not a bug you can fix.

exit-connector-kb.heading: Take this to the official forum with a Debug ID
exit-connector-kb.body: Persistent saving failures are usually translator or site-specific issues the Zotero team debugs from a log. Before posting, capture a Debug ID (Help → Debug Output Logging → Restart with Logging Enabled, reproduce the save, then Submit) — the forum answer time drops dramatically when a Debug ID is attached.

done-save-lesson.heading: Saving works again
done-save-lesson.body: Re-check the basics with lesson 2: Save your first sources from the web.

flows.title: The Zotero tab is missing in Microsoft Word
flows.hint: Separate macOS and Windows paths: reinstall, templates/add-ins, then permissions or the Trust Center.
flows.based_on: C2 (15 questions); rows #46, #138 in the support analysis

q-platform.heading: Which system is Word on?
q-platform.body: The plugin is bundled with Zotero and normally installs itself. When it doesn't, the fix differs by platform.

fix-mac.heading: On macOS: reinstall the add-in, check templates, then permissions
fix-mac.body:
1. Quit Word completely. In Zotero: Settings → Cite → Word Processors → Install Microsoft Word Add-in. Reopen Word and look for the tab.
  2. In Word: Tools → Templates and Add-ins… — confirm Zotero.dotm is listed and ticked under Global Templates and Add-ins. Missing? Re-run step 1 and check that Word's Startup folder is at its default location.
  3. Word opens but says “Word could not communicate with Zotero”, or citing fails with an automation error: grant macOS permission — System Settings → Privacy & Security → allow Zotero where prompted (Automation / Accessibility). This is the managed-laptop case from the support data (row #138). If your organization's IT policy blocks it, IT needs to whitelist Zotero — education can't override an MDM policy, and this tool won't pretend otherwise.
  4. Make sure Word itself is the latest stable version.

fix-windows.heading: On Windows: reinstall, un-disable the add-in, check the Trust Center
fix-windows.body:
1. Quit Word. In Zotero: Edit → Settings → Cite → Word Processors → Install Microsoft Word Add-in. Reopen Word.
  2. In Word: File → Options → Add-ins. Find Zotero.dotm. If it's under Inactive Application Add-ins: Manage → Word Add-ins → Go… → tick Zotero.dotm. If under Disabled Application Add-ins: Manage → Disabled Items → Go… → Enable.
  3. Still hidden? File → Options → Trust Center → Trust Center Settings… — uncheck “Require Application Add-ins to be signed by Trusted Publisher” and “Disable all Application Add-ins”, then restart Word. (Company policy variants of this need IT — that's an environment restriction, not a fixable bug.)
  4. Neither Zotero nor Word should run as administrator — both must run as the same user.

exit-word.heading: The official troubleshooting page covers the remaining cases
exit-word.body: Institutional IT policies, macro settings, Normal.dotm resets and clean reinstalls are documented step by step on Zotero's plugin troubleshooting page. If nothing there fits, post on the forum with your Word version and platform.
exit-word.link_label: Official docs: word processor plugin troubleshooting

done-word.heading: The Zotero tab is in the ribbon
done-word.body: Now insert your first citation: lesson 6: Insert citations and choose a style.

flows.title: Citations show as ADDIN ZOTERO_ITEM codes — or won't update
flows.hint: Two symptoms that look broken but usually aren't — the common one takes five seconds to fix.
flows.based_on: C2/C3 (28 questions combined); rows #58, #139, #140 in the support analysis

q-cite-symptom.heading: Which of these matches your document?
q-cite-symptom.body: Both symptoms look broken. Only one is actually a settings display, and it takes five seconds to fix.

options.label: I see text like { ADDIN ZOTERO_ITEM CSL_CITATION … } instead of citations
A citation (or the bibliography) shows old data after I edited the item in Zotero

fix-codes.heading: Toggle field codes off — your citation data is fine
fix-codes.body:
1. Press Alt+F9 (Windows) or Option-Fn-F9 (Mac) in Word. In LibreOffice: Ctrl+F9. The codes flip back to formatted citations.
  2. If codes keep coming back: Word → Options/Preferences → Advanced (Windows) or View (Mac) → untick “Show field codes instead of their values”.
  3. With Track Changes on, Word may show both versions of a changed citation — accept the change twice and the codes disappear.

Nothing was broken: Zotero stores citations as Word fields, and Word was showing you the machinery.

fix-stale.heading: Refresh — but fix the item in Zotero first
fix-stale.body:
1. Correct the item in Zotero — the author, year or title that is wrong. Never edit the citation text in Word: manual edits block automatic updates.
  2. Back in the document, click Refresh in the Zotero tab. Every citation and the bibliography re-read from Zotero.
  3. Still stale? Someone edited that citation as text. Select it, delete it, and re-insert with Add/Edit Citation, then Refresh.
  4. “Anonymous” in the citation means the item has no author in Zotero — fill one in, then Refresh.

exit-codes-kb.heading: Persistent field-code display goes to the official KB and forum
exit-codes-kb.body: If codes survive a settings change on both counts, the document may have been produced by another tool. The official KB page lists the remaining display settings per platform.

exit-stale-kb.heading: Take the document specifics to the official KB
exit-stale-kb.body: Documents that were converted between formats (Google Docs → Word, .odt → .docx) can lose field links in ways this flow can't diagnose. The KB page covers the remaining cases; the forum is good at converted documents if you say exactly which conversion.

done-cites.heading: Your citations are live again
done-cites.body: Keep the habits that prevent this: edit items in Zotero, click Refresh, and never retype a citation — lesson 8: Fix common citation formatting errors has the full checklist.

flows.title: PDFs or changes won't sync across devices
flows.hint: Four sync symptoms: error messages, files missing on device 2, quota warnings, or repeated conflicts.
flows.based_on: C5 (16 questions); rows #99, #132, #133, #142, #143 in the support analysis

q-sync-symptom.heading: What do you see?
q-sync-symptom.body: Data (items, notes, tags) and files (PDFs) sync separately — the symptom tells you which half to look at.

options.label: A sync error icon or message appears
No error, but a PDF is missing on my other device
Zotero keeps asking to resolve the same conflicts

fix-sync-error.heading: Read the error — it names the problem
fix-sync-error.body:
1. Click the sync error icon (next to the Sync button on desktop, or at the bottom of the items list on mobile). The message is specific.
  2. Username/password errors: re-enter credentials in Settings → Sync → Data Syncing.
  3. “Too many authentication failures” / HTTP 429: you're rate-limited, usually after many rapid retries — wait a few minutes and sync once. If the error mentions API keys, sign out of Zotero syncing and sign back in: in row #99's thread a deleted/stale key kept re-authenticating until the sign-out/in.
  4. Anything else: the error text usually links to a page with the fix — follow it before posting.

fix-file-missing.heading: Was the file ever uploaded? Almost always the answer is no
fix-file-missing.body:
1. Confirm the file opens on the device where it was added.
  2. Sign in at zotero.org and check your online library: is the attachment there? (An attachment item without a file can sync while the file itself never did.)
  3. If the file never uploaded: on the desktop device that has it — Settings → Sync → Reset → Reset File Sync History. Use only that option; the others in that pane are destructive. Then sync and re-check zotero.org.
  4. If it uploaded but device B lacks it: check device B uses the same account and the same file-sync setting (Zotero storage vs. WebDAV can't see each other).
  5. Using linked files (chain icon)? Those don't sync at all by design — convert via Tools → Manage Attachments → Convert Linked Files to Stored Files.

fix-quota.heading: Quota warnings: find what's filling 300 MB, then decide
fix-quota.body:
1. Check your usage at zotero.org storage settings. The free plan includes 300 MB of file storage; data (items, notes) is unlimited and never quota'd.
  2. Recently upgraded a plan? Re-sync the device where the files were added — the upgrade doesn't retro-push; the warning can persist until it does (row #142).
  3. Don't want to pay? Delete unneeded attachments (right-click an item → Remove Attachment… keep the item), or move large PDFs to linked files with your own cloud storage — accepting they won't sync through Zotero.

fix-conflicts.heading: Repeated conflicts: break the loop deliberately
fix-conflicts.body:
1. Sync one device at a time: let device A finish completely before syncing device B. Parallel syncs are the most common cause of a repeating conflict prompt (row #143).
  2. When the dialog appears, pick a version deliberately — don't cancel; cancelled conflicts queue again.
  3. If the same conflict returns after a clean single-device sync, capture a Debug ID (Help → Debug Output Logging) and take it to the forum — that's a genuine bug report, not a setup mistake.

exit-sync-forum.heading: Sync bugs go to the forum with a Debug ID
exit-sync-forum.body: Before posting: Help → Debug Output Logging → Restart with Logging Enabled…, reproduce the sync error, then Submit to get a Debug ID. Include it, plus the error text, in your post.

done-sync.heading: Your library syncs again
done-sync.body: Review the settings decisions in lesson 9: Sync your library across devices — data vs. file syncing is the distinction behind most of these problems.
